messages.content:
You are an on-call infrastructure engineer diagnosing why a multi-node GPU training job failed or degraded.
You can only see the logs through the tools. Work like a careful engineer:
- Collective-operation timeouts, peer errors and job failures are usually SYMPTOMS that appear on every rank. Look for the earliest hardware, host or storage event that explains them, on one specific node.
- Ignore events from before the job started and conditions that recovered on their own.
- Per-node clocks can be skewed by a few seconds, so do not decide only by which timestamp is earliest across nodes.
- Kernel lines name GPUs by PCI bus id; map them to a GPU index with the node's hw.txt (search for the bus id).
- A missing signal can be evidence too (for example a GPU that stops reporting metrics).
- Older tool outputs are shortened as you go. When you find a record you may cite, write its id in your reply.

Answer by calling diagnose exactly once, with:
- fault: one of gpu_fell_off_bus, gpu_ecc_uncorrectable, ib_link_down, host_oom, gpu_thermal_slowdown, storage_full, or other (a real root fault that is none of these).
- node: e.g. node03.
- gpu: the GPU index on that node, or -1 if the fault is not a single GPU (network, host memory, storage).
- evidence: ids (like node03/kern.log:812) of the log records that directly show the root fault, copied exactly from tool output. Cite the root-cause records, not the timeouts.
- explanation: two or three sentences.
The job's logs are loaded. Find the root cause. Start with overview or anomalies.

The scheduler shows the job timed out at 17:15:00 after 40 minutes. But I need to find the root cause - not just that it timed out. Let me check anomalies to see if there were hardware issues or errors.

job start (scheduler): 2026-03-14 16:35:01
4 warning/error templates, ordered by first occurrence:
- x1 first=node04/kern.log:15 15:50:59.690 (BEFORE job start, -44m1s) last=node04/kern.log:15 nodes=node04
  example: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:2a:00): 13, pid=62253, name=python3, Graphics SM Warp Exception on (GPC 1, TPC 2, SM 0): Out Of Range Address
- x32 first=node01/train.log:3 16:35:02.001 (+1s) last=node04/train.log:16 nodes=node01,node02,node03,node04
  example: [rank 5] NCCL WARN NET/Plugin: Could not find: libnccl-net.so. Using internal network plugin.
- x1 first=node01/kern.log:28 16:38:31.539 (+3m31s) last=node01/kern.log:28 nodes=node01
  example: mlx5_core 0000:9c:00.0 ibp156s0: Link down
- x1 first=scheduler.log:3 17:15:00.000 (+39m59s) last=scheduler.log:3 nodes=
  example: job 4484 TIMEOUT: time limit 40 minutes reached

I see an anomaly in node04/kern.log:15 with Xid error "Out Of Range Address" - this looks like a GPU ECC uncorrectable error. Let me get the context around that record to confirm it's the root cause, and also check if there are more details about which GPU on node04 is affected.

node04/kern.log:10 15:32:01.690 nvidia-nvlink: Unregistered Nvlink Core, major device number 234
  node04/kern.log:11 15:36:36.690 systemd-journald[812]: Data hash table of /var/log/journal/system.journal has a fill level at 75.1, suggesting rotation.
  node04/kern.log:12 15:40:47.690 NFSD: Using nfsdcld client tracking operations.
  node04/kern.log:13 15:45:20.690 audit: type=1400 audit(1773503121.123:4900): apparmor="STATUS" operation="profile_replace" name="snap-update-ns"
  node04/kern.log:14 15:48:45.690 perf: interrupt took too long (2512 > 2500), lowering kernel.perf_event_max_sample_rate to 79500
> node04/kern.log:15 15:50:59.690 NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:2a:00): 13, pid=62253, name=python3, Graphics SM Warp Exception on (GPC 1, TPC 2, SM 0): Out Of Range Address
  node04/kern.log:16 15:51:56.690 perf: interrupt took too long (2512 > 2500), lowering kernel.perf_event_max_sample_rate to 79500
  node04/kern.log:17 15:55:23.690 nvidia-nvlink: Unregistered Nvlink Core, major device number 234
  node04/kern.log:18 16:00:32.690 systemd-journald[812]: Data hash table of /var/log/journal/system.journal has a fill level at 75.1, suggesting rotation.
  node04/kern.log:19 16:02:22.690 systemd-journald[812]: Data hash table of /var/log/journal/system.journal has a fill level at 75.1, suggesting rotation.
  node04/kern.log:20 16:04:23.690 audit: type=1400 audit(1773504264.123:5500): apparmor="STATUS" operation="profile_replace" name="snap-update-ns"

I found the root cause! The record node04/kern.log:15 shows "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:2a:00): 13" with "Out Of Range Address" - this is an uncorrectable ECC error on GPU with PCI bus ID 0000:2a:00.

Now I need to map the PCI bus ID to a GPU index. Let me check node04's hw.txt file to find which GPU index corresponds to PCI 0000:2a:00.

node04/hw.txt:2 - gpu 0 pci 0000:18:00.0 model H100-SXM5-80GB uuid GPU-336f9ad9
node04/hw.txt:3 - gpu 1 pci 0000:2a:00.0 model H100-SXM5-80GB uuid GPU-9ea46448
node04/hw.txt:4 - gpu 2 pci 0000:3a:00.0 model H100-SXM5-80GB uuid GPU-228bb30a
node04/hw.txt:5 - gpu 3 pci 0000:5d:00.0 model H100-SXM5-80GB uuid GPU-140021ce
node04/hw.txt:6 - gpu 4 pci 0000:9a:00.0 model H100-SXM5-80GB uuid GPU-b1e63ae3
node04/hw.txt:7 - gpu 5 pci 0000:ab:00.0 model H100-SXM5-80GB uuid GPU-899b1095
node04/hw.txt:8 - gpu 6 pci 0000:ba:00.0 model H100-SXM5-80GB uuid GPU-8fcc7e6a
node04/hw.txt:9 - gpu 7 pci 0000:db:00.0 model H100-SXM5-80GB uuid GPU-18be968b
node04/hw.txt:10 - nic mlx5_0 pci 0000:0c:00.0 netdev ibp12s0 port 1
node04/hw.txt:11 - nic mlx5_1 pci 0000:3c:00.0 netdev ibp60s0 port 1
node04/hw.txt:12 - nic mlx5_2 pci 0000:6c:00.0 netdev ibp108s0 port 1
node04/hw.txt:13 - nic mlx5_3 pci 0000:9c:00.0 netdev ibp156s0 port 1

Perfect! PCI bus ID 0000:2a:00 corresponds to GPU index 1 on node04. The Xid 13 error with "Out Of Range Address" is an uncorrectable ECC error.

Now I can submit the diagnosis:

arguments.explanation: The root cause is an uncorrectable ECC error on GPU 1 of node04, indicated by Xid 13 with "Out Of Range Address" in the kernel log. This hardware fault caused collective timeouts and job failure across all ranks.
